_meta.scope: Every assigned bony-fish label except broad residual Actinopterygii/Gadiformes/Marine fishes nei, plus Dosidicus gigas/Doryteuthis gahi/Teuthida. Includes allzero2019 catches and retained labels.
_meta.source_definition_interpretation: Table1 group6 includes small and medium pelagic fishes nonexhaustively, with no numeric length cutoff;7 lists Seriolella caerulea[misspelledcearulea]/punctata without an including qualifier. Do not equate its title with a full demersal residual. Original Hoki Table 1 and prose use juveniles <3 and adults ≥3 years; a secondary >3 transcription is not the operative boundary.

mmc1.S1: Time series used for calibration process
mmc1.S2: Vulnerabilities estimated in calibration process (yellow values)

mmc2.S3: Pedigree values of input data for model of Chilean Patagonia ecosystem
mmc2.S5: Defined pedigree options/values for P/B and Q/B
mmc2.S6: Defined pedigree options/values for diet composition

supplements.membership_implication: S2/S3 call6 Other pelagic fish but provide no expanded species inventory. Present supplements contradict a blanket S1–S7 absent statement; this review makes no parameter/diet/calibration changes.

_meta.allocation_limits: W1 High is unsplit allocation only, not mapping truth. W4/W9 are explicit native1980 source proxies with time/regional/catchability assumptions. Baseline exact retained weights preserved; pooled Hoki does not establish grenadier ages.

paper.locator: Neira et al. Table 1, PDF page 4; Section 2.2
paper.supports: Group 6 openly includes small and medium pelagic fishes; group 7 lists two Seriolella species; other fish groups name species; Hoki table uses <3 and >=3 years. Original Table 1 and prose use adults ≥3 years; >3 is a secondary transcription discrepancy.

supp1.locator: S1 Time series used for calibration process; S2 Vulnerabilities estimated in calibration process (yellow values)
supp1.supports: S2 uses Other pelagic fish for group6; no expanded species composition. S1 is calibration time series, not a new membership inventory.

supp2.locator: S3 pedigree input table; S4 biomass; S5 production/consumption; S6 diet; S7 yield pedigree options
supp2.supports: S3 also says Other pelagic fish; S4–S7 describe pedigree choices, not extra biological group definitions.

norman.supports: Adult Normanichthys is a schooling pelagic fish up to11cm total length in southeast Pacific, with copepod diet; evidence is not limited to larvae.

larimus_stri.locator: Species prose; Water Column Position and Habitat fields
larimus_stri.supports: Coastal fish1–273m, at least30cm, nearbottom/midwater and softbottom; Pelagic is an imported FishBase field and does not erase bottom association.

imarpe_guide.locator: Zavalaga et al.2018 Guide to trawl fishes, species Larimus p13; Polydactylus p12; Ctenosciaena p14
imarpe_guide.material_read: Search-result species text read; full web open failed
imarpe_guide.supports: Larimus occurs over coastal sandy/muddy/rocky bottoms40–60m; regional guide supports bottom shelf ecology. The demersal20–325m text on p14 belongs Ctenosciaena, not Larimus.

imarpe2018.locator: Tumbes quarterly report; Table3 demersal/coastal fishes
imarpe2018.material_read: Search-result table and surrounding text read
imarpe2018.supports: Larimus16–27cmTL527fish and Cynoscion/Paralabrax measured under demersal/coastal sampling. This is observed regional catch context, not a2019 mass allocation.

redbait.supports: Emmelichthys nitidus is schooling pelagic fish up to50cm; juveniles near surface and adults deeper near seabed with nightly ascent; SEPacific E.n.cyanescens included.

stromateus.locator: Species prose and structured habitat/diet fields
stromateus.supports: Stromateus30cm, coastal pelagic in prose; structured benthopelagic/nearbottom and pelagic prey fields qualify confidence.

galaxias.locator: Chilean Ministry species account life cycle
galaxias.supports: Galaxias is diadromous: marine planktonic larvae/juveniles and freshwater adults; provider large reef tag is inconsistent. No caughtstage fraction supplied.

galaxias_plos.supports: Galaxias larval marine dispersal is epipelagic in Magellanic province; does not identify stage or habitat of these landings.

coelo.supports: Coelorinchus chilensis benthopelagic260–1480m, at least48cmTL, Peru6°26S→Chile38°08S; long dorsal/anal series and tapering body illustrated. Adjacent200–700m text is another species.

coelo_ifop.supports: Regional species body25–40cmLT and very long second dorsal/anal fin series; no caught-age composition inferred.

macrourid_feeding.supports: Macrourids benthopelagic; Coelorinchus benthic prey foraging. This genus-level feeding inference is not a Chilean measured diet.

hoki_ecology.supports: M.magellanicus gadiform shelf/slope fish60–600m in southernChile/SWAtlantic; historical Merlucciidae classification is not proof of modern Macrouridae identity.

hoki_morph.locator: FAO Hakes2004 Macruronus genus diagnosis printed11; account13–14
hoki_morph.supports: Macruronus has compressed body with tapering tail. Old catalogue lumps magellanicus under novaezelandiae; this review preserves current exact catch key and source species identity.

salilota.supports: Salilota is southern Chile gadiform demersal fleet species co-caught with hake,hoki,whiting,kingklip. It is not an explicit source-group member.

salilota_fao.supports: Benthopelagic40→1000+m southernChile/Patagonia, least50cmTL; depth increase with size. Source whiting pelagic role is less fitting.

hake.supports: Southern hake has shelf/estuary/deep habitat variation and progressively piscivorous diet, relevant when comparing weak cod-like analogues.

selene.supports: Selene peruviana is demersal on sandy bottoms1–50m, up to85cm; contradicts provider smallpelagic tag.

decapterus.supports: Decapterus macrosoma35cm pelagic coastal/oceanic and Baja→Chile; direct generic source6 fit.

seriola.supports: Large250cm reef/watercolumn/nearbottom fish; juvenile/offshore and adult bottom roles make source6 versus7 uncertain.

seriola_riv.material_read: Full search-result primary institutional account read
seriola_riv.supports: Demersal and pelagic, mainly oceanic; at least160cm/common60cm. Caribbean scope does not establish Chilean caughtstage composition.

seriolella_v.material_read: Full primary institutional web account read
seriolella_v.supports: 65cm coastal/nearcoastal pelagic Colombia→Chile; fits source6 generic small/medium pelagic criterion, not the two other named species in7.

fao_shared.locator: Zuzunaga FAO Peru shared stocks chapter, jack mackerel and sardine sections
fao_shared.supports: Trachurus is schooling pelagic up to70cm; Sardinops schooling coastal pelagic around33cm in Peru/Chile. No2019 size-frequency allocation claimed.

scomber.locator: FAO synopsis1572000 abstract and section1.3.1 printed4/PDF10
scomber.supports: S.japonicus coastal pelagic, common30cm and maximum usually50cm fork length; FL is recorded as FL and not converted to a TLcutoff.

auxis.locator: FAO biological synopsis of Auxis thazard/rochei, size sections
auxis.supports: Bullet/frigate tunas have small/medium observed body sizes; foreign distributions are not2019 regional caughtmass proportions.

sarda.locator: FAO Sarda synopsis Table23 southern S.c.chiliensis Chile1968–69
sarda.supports: Observed southern bonito40–73cm but species can larger; local old sample cannot prove entire2019 mass meets generic small/medium scope.

odontesthes.supports: O.regia exclusively marine small coastal forage fish Peru→southernChile; sampled adult sizes inmmTL, no2019 caughtmass fractions.

orange.locator: FAO deepwater resources chapter orange roughy section
orange.supports: Orange roughy deep seamount aggregates often>800m; database bathypelagic tag does not imply shallow smallpelagic guild identity.

gempylids.locator: Nakamura/Parin FAO1993 catalogue pp52–55,106–107; ecology sectionpp9–10
gempylids.material_read: Full primary catalogue species text read
gempylids.supports: Oilfish nearbottom oceanic slope, snoek shelf benthopelagic/midwater schooling, cutlassfish shelf watercolumn and bottom movements; all require weak transfer here.

thyrsites.locator: Duarte et al.2007 Chile neritic diet study pp408–409
thyrsites.supports: Neritic Chile snoek eats schooling pelagic fishes and squid; observed47–102cmFL. Trophic relation alone does not create exact source6 membership.

dosidicus.locator: Alegre et al.2014 Northern Humboldt squid trophic study
dosidicus.supports: Dosidicus active squid predator with pelagic trophic links; no model cephalopod guild or direct fish membership.

cephalopods.locator: FAO CephalopodsVol2 Doryteuthis gahi printed59; Dosidicus printed301–304
cephalopods.material_read: Doryteuthis account search text; Dosidicus split PDF full text read
cephalopods.supports: Gahi medium neritic shelf squid, max400mm mantle length; ML not TL. Dosidicus large mobile oceanic squid. Figure88 is a figure number, not gahi page88.

doryteuthis.supports: Doryteuthis gahi formerly Loligo gahi, neritic SEPacific/SWAtlantic continental shelf squid; no caughtstage allocation inferred.

tam.supports: NorthernHumboldt165000km² donor: smallpelagic Anchoa, butterfish Stromateus, separate jumbo/othercephalopod guilds; demersal/flatfish pools. Different region/time and no focal squid-guild equivalent.
